selected_title: An attained eventual reality threshold for a growing quartic arithmetic transform
editorial_decision: One sustained global paper should combine saddle estimates, exact arithmetic obstruction, polynomial approximation, attainment, confinement and collision. Do not split the easy endpoint topology into a purported complete proof of the global theorem.

definitions.transform: H_t(z)=integral_0^infinity exp(t*u^4)*K(u)*cos(u*z) du; t is real, z is complex. Growing positive quartic tilt, not exp(-t*u^4).
definitions.approximation: LP(t) means a sequence of real polynomials splitting over R converges to H_t locally uniformly on the whole complex plane.
definitions.starts: S={T in R: for every t>=T, LP(t)}; A=inf S. S is a set of eventual starting times, not by definition the set {t:LP(t)}.

exact_verified_scope: S is nonempty, A is finite and A>8; S=[A,infinity).
For every t>=A, all complex zeros of the actual H_t are real and LP(t) holds.
There is a nonreal zero for every t in some open neighborhood of 8.
For every epsilon>0 there is some s in (A-epsilon,A) and a nonreal zero of H_s.
A single finite B confines every nonreal zero for every t>=1.
There are s_n<A tending to A and nonreal zeros z_n tending to a real threshold zero.
At A there is a positive real zero of finite analytic multiplicity at least two.
For every sufficiently large t, every zero is real and simple. This is not endpoint simplicity.
prohibited_strengthenings: Do not assert {t: all zeros of H_t are real}=[A,infinity); earlier isolated reality times or intervals have not been excluded by the eventual-start statement.
Do not assert that every t<A has a nonreal zero, that all t>A have only simple zeros, or that the endpoint multiplicity is exactly two.
Do not assert a continuously tracked zero trajectory, first-exit/reentry history, numerical upper threshold or RH implication.
Do not replace a common stationary center in bounded and far regions by unrelated fixed-time limits.
Do not treat fixed-frequency cosine approximation, model-saddle existence or a certificate for a truncated kernel as the actual whole-plane theorem.

Attainment from compact-time continuity: For s_n tending to t with LP(s_n), choose for each n one real split polynomial Q_n approximating H_{s_n} within 1/(n+1) on |z|<=n. This is possible by local uniform polynomial convergence at that fixed time.

On every fixed compact K, eventually K is inside |z|<=n. Compact-uniform continuity in time gives sup_K|H_{s_n}-H_t| tending to zero. The triangle inequality proves Q_n tends locally uniformly to H_t; hence LP(t).

For each t>A, infimum approximation gives T in S with T<t, so LP(t). Apply the preceding diagonal argument to t_n=A+1/(n+1) to get LP(A). Thus A is in S, and the infimum and upward-closed definition give S=[A,infinity).
Nonreal zeros immediately below the endp: Fix epsilon>0 and T=A-epsilon/2. Since T is not in S, some t>=T fails LP(t). Since every t>=A satisfies LP(t), this chosen t is less than A.
The exact equivalence LP(t) iff all zeros of H_t are real then supplies a nonreal zero. This proves existence at some time in (A-epsilon,A), not at every earlier time.
Confinement and compactness: Choose a late time T0 after which all zeros are real. The bounded-time far-zero theorem provides a single radius B valid for 1<=t<=T0. Any nonreal zero at time t>=1 is either in that bounded-time disk or contradicts late-time reality. Thus one B works for all t>=1.
Choose s_n in (A-1/(n+1),A) with nonreal zero z_n. Since A>8, all these times are >=1. The common B puts z_n in a compact disk; select a convergent subsequence.
Joint continuity gives H_A(w)=0 at its limit, and threshold reality gives Im(w)=0. No escape to infinity or unproved path tracking is used.
The collision derivative: Suppose c=H_A prime(w) is nonzero. Joint continuity of the derivative gives a convex disk around the real w and a time neighborhood on which |H_s prime(q)-c|<=|c|/2.
For z,zbar in that disk, integrate the derivative along their segment. The triangle inequality applied after subtracting c(z-zbar) gives |H_s(z)-H_s(zbar)| >= |c|*|z-zbar|/2.
For the convergent nonreal zeros, conjugation symmetry makes both z_n and zbar_n zeros. They are distinct, contradicting this lower bound. Hence H_A prime(w)=0.

H_A(0)>0 excludes w=0. Evenness reflects a negative real w to a positive zero, with the derivative reflected oddly. The entire H_A is nonzero, so the order at that zero is finite and at least two. Exact double multiplicity does not follow.
Common-center whole-plane assembly: Let B(u)=4*pi*exp(4u). Choose M=2*exp(64) and R=max(N,120021), where N is the uniform far theorem cutoff in the stationary-center parameter.
For all sufficiently late t the bounded-ratio theorem supplies one actual real stationary center u>=R such that every zero in |z|<=M*B(u) is real and simple.

For the complementary region |z|>=2*exp(64)*B(u), the uniform far theorem applies to this same u and t. The regions cover the whole plane. Far real-zero simplicity is then added with the same cutoff and even reflection for negative real frequencies.
This is a valid assembly only after both actual uniform analytic theorems have full proofs; it is not a replacement for those analytic proofs.
Balanced amplitude identity: Given a nonzero complex center amplitude a and an analytic primitive P with fixed center value zero, let Pstar(z)=conj(P(conj(z))). Define E(z)=|a| exp((P(z)+Pstar(z))/2) and Phi(z)=arg(a)+(P(z)-Pstar(z))/(2i).
Then (a exp(P(z))+conj(a) exp(Pstar(z)))/2=E(z) cos(Phi(z)), and the sum of the two amplitude norms is 2|E(z)| cosh(Im(Phi(z))).
These exact identities convert relative pair-integral error into the weighted cosine error used in the local zero lemma. The argument of a is fixed; no varying principal argument is differentiated.

remaining_human_proof_obligations.requirement: Reconstruct all model-to-actual corrections, branch geometry and uniform quantifiers. The model phase t*z^4+9*z-pi*exp(4*z) is not the full log kernel.
Give complete contour deformation, local Gaussian error, tails and vertical endpoint budgets. Horizontal absolute bounds alone cannot replace the rotating far Gaussian estimate.
Reconstruct phase straightening and buffered derivative estimates turning weighted cosine error into exact real/simple zeros, not merely nearby zeros.

Explain 160 cells, 4 theta terms, degree-15 quadrature and all actual-integral error budgets. At x=632083/10000, time 8, the actual real Laguerre expression is less than -2/10^20. A float experiment is not this certificate.

Explain the actual growth bound C_t exp(|z|^(3/2)), paired canonical product and normalization, or cite a precise classical theorem with every hypothesis checked. Do not assume a converse to Hurwitz without the growth input.

primary_literature.author: N. G. de Bruijn
primary_literature.title: The roots of trigonometric integrals
primary_literature.review: Primary repository search text and bibliographic record consulted; full fetch timed out. No detailed theorem comparison based on unread pages is claimed.

primary_literature.author: Charles M. Newman
primary_literature.title: Fourier Transforms with Only Real Zeros
primary_literature.review: Primary article text inspected, especially Theorem 1 and its explicitly quadratic multiplier exp(delta*u^2). It does not justify quartic monotone propagation. No general priority conclusion for the actual quartic package follows.

novelty: UNRESOLVED. The eventual-start distinction must be kept when comparing with quadratic de Bruijn-Newman constants. No independent new-research claim is made.

    ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in atTop, ∀ u : ℝ, 65536*(M+7) ≤ u →
      RiemannQuarticSaddleTimes.phaseSlope t u=0 → ∀ x : ℝ,
      |x| ≤ M*RiemannQuarticTransitionSaddle.realScale u →

def polynomialLimitStarts : Set ℝ

theorem polynomial_limit_of_time_sequence (s : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℝ)
    (hs : Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 t))
    (hP : ∀ n, ∃ P : ℕ → ℝ[X], (∀ j, (P j).Splits) ∧
      TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
        (fun j z => ((P j).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).eval z) (flow (s n)) atTop univ) :
    ∃ Q : ℕ → ℝ[X], (∀ n, (Q n).Splits) ∧

        (fun n z => ((Q n).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).eval z) (flow t) atTop univ

theorem actual_starts_eq_Ici_infimum :
    polynomialLimitStarts = Ici (sInf polynomialLimitStarts)

theorem actual_polynomial_limit_iff_real_zeros (t : ℝ) :
    (∃ P : ℕ → ℝ[X], (∀ n, (P n).Splits) ∧
      TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn
        (fun n z => ((P n).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).eval z) (flow t) atTop univ) ↔
    ∀ z : ℂ, flow t z = 0 → z.im = 0

theorem nonreal_zeros_arbitrarily_before_threshold (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, sInf polynomialLimitStarts-ε < t ∧ t < sInf polynomialLimitStarts ∧
      ∃ z : ℂ, flow t z = 0 ∧ z.im ≠ 0

theorem uniform_far_zeros_real (T : ℝ) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, 1 ≤ t → t ≤ T →
      ∀ z : ℂ, B ≤ ‖z‖ → RiemannQuarticFlow.flow t z = 0 → z.im = 0

theorem bounded_nonreal_zeros_all_times_ge_one :
    ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, 1 ≤ t →
      ∀ z : ℂ, flow t z = 0 → z.im ≠ 0 → ‖z‖ < B

theorem exists_convergent_nonreal_zeros_before_threshold :
    ∃ (s : ℕ → ℝ) (z : ℕ → ℂ) (w : ℂ),
      Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 (sInf polynomialLimitStarts)) ∧
      Tendsto z atTop (𝓝 w) ∧
      (∀ n, s n < sInf polynomialLimitStarts ∧ flow (s n) (z n) = 0 ∧ (z n).im ≠ 0) ∧
      flow (sInf polynomialLimitStarts) w = 0 ∧ w.im = 0

theorem derivative_zero_of_nonreal_zero_limit (s : ℕ → ℝ) (z : ℕ → ℂ)
    (τ : ℝ) (w : ℂ) (hs : Tendsto s atTop (𝓝 τ)) (hz : Tendsto z atTop (𝓝 w))
    (hw : w.im = 0) (hzero : ∀ n, flow (s n) (z n) = 0)
    (hnon : ∀ n, (z n).im ≠ 0) : deriv (flow τ) w = 0

theorem exists_positive_finite_multiple_zero_at_threshold :
    ∃ x : ℝ, 0 < x ∧ flow (sInf polynomialLimitStarts) (x : ℂ) = 0 ∧
      deriv (flow (sInf polynomialLimitStarts)) (x : ℂ) = 0 ∧
      2 ≤ analyticOrderAt (flow (sInf polynomialLimitStarts)) (x : ℂ) ∧
      analyticOrderAt (flow (sInf polynomialLimitStarts)) (x : ℂ) ≠ ⊤
